records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A qualified integrator or assessor should document repeated paid handover failures on one named stack, show that current CE/PLM tools cannot ingest the required identifiers, commit to a paid pilot with defined system access and liability boundaries, and demonstrate across several releases that mappings are reusable, implementation hours fall, activation pricing is accepted, and gross-margin/payback assumptions survive channel economics.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not yet proven to be an uncovered, recurring, budgeted problem; that single uncertainty simultaneously constrains willingness to pay, partner distribution, reusable economics, and defensibility.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Safexpert already advertises change tracking, traceable histories, technical-document workflows, and reusable projects, while CEM4 and CEDOC offer overlapping capabilities at established price points; the research found no direct evidence that PLC or safety-program provenance ingestion is missing or separately budgeted.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A prepaid pilot contract from a converter plus written permission and technical access from at least one brand endpoint, accompanied by a measured baseline of duplicate evidence work, proof that the required flow is not supported economically by the incumbent platform, actual connector delivery hours and gross margin, and follow-on evidence that the same connector can be reused for a second converter or brand without bespoke rebuilding.
records.primary_score_limiter: The critical commercial control point is not owned: a sale requires converter budget plus brand endpoint permission, yet the research establishes neither access nor an interoperability gap that incumbent PPWR and specification-platform APIs leave open, making repeatable distribution and connector reuse doubtful.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PPWR Connect already combines converter positioning with ERP/API connectivity at EUR 29-299 per month, while Recyda and Specright already provide supplier-data collection, component mapping, audit trails, declarations, and APIs; this directly undermines the premise that a valuable neutral handoff layer is missing.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid Polish portfolio pilots covering a meaningful forward pipeline, with retained renewal intent and site-level observations of screening time, gate accuracy, full-audit conversion, buyer reservations, completed sales, removal and logistics costs, contribution margin, CAC payback, and written legal and insurance acceptance of the exact operator-of-record contract flow.
records.primary_score_limiter: The redesign depends simultaneously on customers paying a recurring screening retainer and on sparse pre-audit site data predicting net recoverable value accurately enough to improve economics; neither dependency is supported by the bound evidence.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: JRC reports roughly EUR 3000-5000 audit costs for demolition projects up to EUR 300000 while finding economic effectiveness uncertain, especially for smaller projects; this directly challenges whether screening can surface enough surplus value to fund the audit-and-coordination layer consistently.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid pilot with a registered independent processor that mandates use by at least three recurring generator streams, grants lawful continuing record rights, records actual sales and onboarding cost, and demonstrates conversion or renewal at a price supported by measured labor, rejection, audit, or recall savings and a defensible contribution margin.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no direct evidence that an independent processor will simultaneously pay the proposed price, mandate supplier use, renew the product, and grant durable record rights; those four conditions underpin revenue, distribution, retention, and the proposed data moat.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: IUNGO already sources and processes food-sector streams in Poland, while Trotec and FeedValid bundle containers, transport, weighing, registration, processing, data, and compliance support, indicating that the relevant workflow is commonly integrated with physical operations rather than purchased as a standalone software layer.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots across several independent suppliers showing recurrent correction or launch work, measured hours and first-pass outcomes versus self-service, annual model-family frequency and retention, signed laboratory or distributor referral terms, and cohort unit economics covering CAC, specialist cost, gross margin, payback, and renewal would support a higher score.
records.primary_score_limiter: The opportunity lacks evidence of repeat willingness to pay and a scalable acquisition route in a potentially small Polish wedge, while suppliers and stronger channel holders can use or internalise the free official workflow.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: List ZUM placement is free and directly available to authorised suppliers, evidence routes have been simplified for several categories, EPREL already supplies workflows and APIs, and an adjacent provider already sells overlapping documentation support.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots in one repeatable machine class should show the baseline rate and cost of as-built divergence, successful secure ingestion of PLC and safety-program version evidence, a material reduction in handover time or defects versus incumbent workflows, buyer willingness to pay at the proposed price, bounded onboarding and review hours, a repeatable assessor-led acquisition channel, and renewal or repeat-handover behavior.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed provenance wedge is not demonstrated to be missing from incumbent CE or engineering systems, so buyers may see a separate, integration-heavy release layer as duplicative; this compounds weak differentiation with slow distribution and service-heavy economics.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Safexpert already advertises change tracking, traceable histories, reusable projects, teamwork, standards monitoring, and technical-documentation workflows, while CEM4, CEDOC, and Pilz add low-priced software and expert or end-to-end services; the research found no direct evidence that automatic PLC and safety-program provenance is an uncovered, budgeted gap.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid converter pilot with multiple independently participating brand customers showing quantified duplicate-request reduction, acceptable evidence-sharing permissions, successful writes into existing PLM or specification systems, repeat usage after a packaging change, willingness to pay materially above low-cost alternatives, and a side-by-side gap incumbents cannot readily serve.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point and advantage are not differentiated from well-funded or low-cost incumbents, while the converter neither owns the brand's conformity decision nor has demonstrated authority to make customers adopt a shared rail.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PPWR Connect already sells converter-oriented technical files, declarations, component graphs, and ERP/API access for EUR 29-299 per month, while Recyda, Specright, and VINQ collectively demonstrate supplier collection, component mapping, audit trails, declarations, integrations, and expert validation; this directly contradicts a broad unserved-workflow or premium-pricing thesis.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A written conformity opinion allocating the component inside a certified partner's perimeter; a signed partner agreement stating API fees, revenue share, service levels, indemnities, support ownership, and durable channel access; and at least one paid Polish TMS pilot documenting mapping effort, implementation time, electronic-consignment volume, buyer price, gross margin, sales cycle, and expansion intent.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business does not control its regulatory perimeter or route to market: it needs a certified partner that can dictate access, margins, support obligations, or replacement, while buyer adoption is voluntary and incumbent platforms already offer integrations.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The 9 July 2027 obligation applies to authorities accepting compliant electronic data, while operators may continue using paper, so the apparent compliance deadline does not compel TMS vendors or carriers to buy the component.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Signed and paid engagements from at least three independent Polish owners or demolition contractors across a representative pipeline of roughly twenty sites, with site-level evidence on recoverable value, field and specialist cost, inventory time, buyer-match and completed-sale rates, cancellations, contribution margin, CAC/payback, and repeat pipeline, plus written Polish legal and insurer guidance defining eligible component classes and the product-versus-waste and BDO contract flow.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence yet that enough Polish owners will pay an audit fee on sites with sufficient recoverable value to cover specialist-heavy delivery, buyer acquisition, and deadline risk, so attractive repeat economics remain unestablished.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: JRC reports audit costs of roughly EUR 3000-5000 for demolition projects up to EUR 300000 while finding effectiveness and economic benefit uncertain and warning of disproportionate burden for small projects; because the audit is not generally mandated, this directly challenges the payer case.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Ten documented SME or buyer cases where bundled supplier certificates fail a specific site, customer, or reporting-period requirement, together with a registry-capable partner's signed pilot terms confirming lawful data and confirmation access, pricing and revenue share, expected manual exception workload, and measurable CAC, payback, retention, and volume economics.
records.primary_score_limiter: The entities required for registry access and distribution already bundle the core outcome, can absorb the reconciliation feature, and retain most of the bargaining power, leaving willingness to pay and durable margin unproven.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Axpo says renewable-origin coverage is provided to a Polish SME base of nearly 40000 customers without additional or hidden fees, directly contradicting a meaningful standalone subscription for ordinary SME guarantee-of-origin evidence.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid multi-cycle corridor pilot in which one registered processor conditionally commits capacity and at least three generators renew at a stated recurring price, with observed tonnes, transport and testing costs, rejection rates, acquisition effort, gross contribution, record usage after the first match, no bypass, and written regulatory and insurance acceptance of the platform's limited role.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business has not shown that either party will pay for and repeatedly use a standalone record after matching, while integrated processors already own the operational relationship and can bundle or copy the software layer.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Long-standing and expanding direct operators such as IUNGO, Trotec, and FeedValid already combine sourcing with containers, weighing, processing, logistics, data, and compliance support, indicating that the customer's valued solution is operationally integrated rather than a thin exchange.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed integration or reseller commitment from a Polish rental-software, dealer, or insurer channel, plus repeated paid pilots showing that currently underserved fleets complete the workflow, recover materially more damage or save measurable labour, retain at the revised pricing, and produce viable CAC, support cost, channel share, and payback economics.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposal has no demonstrated right to win against an exact low-priced standalone substitute and several embedded incumbents, while its only plausible distribution and retention mechanism depends on uncommitted system-of-record channels.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: HireCheck already sells the core standalone proposition—timestamped and GPS-tagged photos, signatures, inspection history, rental-software integration, and one-click claim packs—with its 100-item year-two price around 417 PLN monthly; InTempo and other platforms additionally embed similar functions directly in the rental workflow.
